meta.title: Write your own agent skill
meta.goal: After this you can write a SKILL.md your agent finds on its own, and link two skills into one workflow.

criterion.text: Get 6 of the 7 questions right, including what makes a skill fire.

options: The words in each skill's description
The name of each skill's folder
How long each skill's file is
The order the skills were installed in
steps.feedback: The agent reads the one-line description of every skill and matches it against your request. That line is the trigger. Everything else is a label.

misconception.1: The folder name is only a label. Renaming the folder changes nothing about when the skill runs.
misconception.2: Length does not matter. A short, clear description beats a long one.
misconception.3: Install order is not a signal. The description is the only thing matched.

steps.prompt: Move the two sliders and watch the chance the agent fires.

widget.caption: Words you really type add about 12 points each. Vague words take about 9 away.

steps.prompt: Drag each description into the right side. Which lines could an agent match against your words?

items.text: verify every link on a page

steps.feedback: The agent matches your words against the description. Words you really type, like check links or verify, are matchable. Words like helper or useful match nothing, so the skill stays quiet.
steps.misconception: It feels safer to describe a skill in general terms. But a general description gives the agent nothing to match, so the skill almost never fires.

steps.feedback: The name is a label and must match its folder. The description is the trigger. disable-model-invocation keeps the agent's hands off until you ask. Each step ends when it is done, so the agent knows where it is.
steps.misconception: It is easy to swap the name and the description. Only the description makes the skill fire; the name is just a label.

steps.prompt: Flip the switch and watch what the agent does.

steps.caption: This is what disable-model-invocation does: the skill waits for you, and while it waits it is not in the agent's list, so it costs nothing.

steps.feedback: Set disable-model-invocation: true in the frontmatter. The agent then leaves the skill alone until you type its name. Use it for anything hard to undo, like sending mail or deleting files, and for a run you start on purpose, like a release checklist. A skill with the key set is not in the agent's list at all, so it costs nothing while you work on something else.
steps.misconception: Many people try deleting the description instead. The key that does the job is disable-model-invocation.

options: Decide the one thing it does
Try it on a real request
steps.feedback: One job first, because it decides everything else. The description next, because that is the trigger. Then the steps. Then run it on a real request to see if it fires.
steps.misconception: Most people start with the steps. If the skill is trying to do too much, no amount of good steps will save it.

steps.prompt: Which of these make an agent more likely to use your skill? Pick all that apply.
options: A description that uses the words you really type
A body so long that the steps are buried
A name that matches its folder
steps.feedback: The agent matches your words against the description, so use the words you type. One clear job makes the skill easy to pick. A name that matches its folder keeps the skill findable.

misconception.2: A long body pushes the steps down, and the agent starts skipping them. Move the bulk into a file the skill points to.

options: The first skill tells the agent to call the second one, by name
Both skills sit in the same folder
The second skill lists the first one in its description
The agent works it out from the file order
steps.feedback: A skill hands off by telling the agent to call the other one and naming it, for example: Call the Skill tool with "442-create-roadmap". Nothing else links them.

misconception.1: Sharing a folder does not link skills. The hand-off is a line in the first skill's steps that names the second.
misconception.3: The agent does not guess from file order. Write the hand-off down, or it will not happen.
